- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for the next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model tends to lag behind true trend; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 7–14 days to catch mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is rising; apply +2–4% bias to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.5), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days to reflect sentiment shift.
